instances.Gold_Response:
He told me the truth about Ariana.

He said their sister Ariana had been attacked by Muggle boys when she was little, which drove her magic inward and left her unstable and frightened. Their father, Percival, attacked the Muggles in revenge, was sent to Azkaban, and the family pretended Ariana was just “sick” so no one would lock her up in St Mungo’s.

Kendra moved them to Godric’s Hollow and spent her life looking after Ariana until, during one of Ariana’s uncontrolled outbursts, Kendra was killed. After that, Albus had to stay home to look after Ariana and resented it, right up until Grindelwald arrived. Albus and Grindelwald started dreaming about wizard domination “for the greater good,” planning to take Ariana with them, until Aberforth confronted them.

The three of them—Albus, Grindelwald, and Aberforth—ended up duelling, Ariana tried to stop it, and a stray curse killed her. None of them knew whose spell it was. Aberforth said Albus never really got over it, and that Grindelwald ran away, leaving Albus with the guilt and the legend everyone chose to believe instead of the truth.

instances.Gold_Response:
I remembered it all really clearly: a dark, creepy room with a fire, Wormtail crouched there snivelling, and that cold, high voice coming from the chair — Voldemort’s voice — talking to him.

Wormtail was terrified, calling him “my Lord” every other word, trying to wriggle out of something. He kept saying the plan could be changed, that they didn’t have to use me, that they could use some other wizard instead. Voldemort wouldn’t hear it. He was furious with Wormtail, saying he’d made a mistake but that it hadn’t ruined everything.

They talked about Bertha Jorkins — that Wormtail had run into her by accident, that she’d been useful, and that she was dead now. Voldemort said they’d need one more murder, and that there was a faithful servant of his already at Hogwarts who would help them. And they were definitely planning to kill me in the end — Voldemort said he would deal with me himself when he was ready.

Wormtail just sounded more and more scared, and Voldemort kept mocking him, calling him useless and cowardly. Then the snake came in, and they realised an old Muggle had overheard them. Voldemort killed him while Wormtail watched, and that was when my scar hurt so much it woke me up.

instances.Gold_Response:
Ron isn’t here anymore.

Things had been getting worse between us for days. We were all hungry and tired, but Ron was taking it the hardest. His arm was still bad from being Splinched, he kept worrying about his family, and that bloody locket seemed to twist everything any of us said. He started snapping more and more, especially about food and about the fact that we hadn’t found another Horcrux yet.

He kept going on about how Dumbledore hadn’t given us enough, that I didn’t have a real plan, that we were just wandering around for nothing. We had a huge row last night after he’d been listening to the radio again. He said I didn’t care that his family were in danger, that I didn’t know what it was like to have a proper family to lose. I lost my temper and shouted back, and it all just exploded from there.

In the end he said he was leaving, with or without Hermione. Hermione chose to stay with me. Ron Disapparated, and he didn’t come back. Hermione was in pieces afterward, and we moved camp today.

We came out of the lift onto this cold, black–tiled corridor on Level Nine and found a single black door marked “Department of Mysteries.”  

When we went through it, we were in this weird circular room with a black floor and walls and a bunch of identical doors, lit by blue flames. As soon as one of the doors shut, the whole room spun around so you couldn’t tell which door was which.  

We realised we’d have to try them one by one to find the place I’d seen in my dream, so Hermione started marking the doors with fiery crosses. The first door we tried took us into a room full of ticking clocks and that bell jar with the hummingbird egg, and from there we kept testing rooms, trying to get to the aisles of glass spheres.

It was the day of the Gryffindor–Ravenclaw match. Ron finally played like... well, like a proper Keeper, saved loads of goals, and I caught the Snitch, so we absolutely thrashed Ravenclaw.

After that we had a massive party in the common room. Everyone was singing the new “Weasley Is Our King” song, Fred and George were showing off, butterbeer everywhere, that sort of thing. Hermione came back from the staffroom and told us Umbridge had tried to throw Trelawney out but Dumbledore had let her stay in the castle and was bringing in a new Divination teacher.

The party went on for ages until McGonagall finally came in and broke it up. I went up to bed, still thinking how brilliant Ron had been and how we might actually win the Cup, and fell asleep. That was just before I had the vision about Voldemort and Rookwood.

Ron had the locket on and we were all on edge, hungry, cold, and getting nowhere with finding Horcruxes. He started going on about how we had no plan, how Dumbledore had left me useless clues, how I didn’t know what I was doing, and how his family and Ginny might be in danger while we were just “wandering around.”

I snapped back that he could go back to them if he wanted, that nobody was forcing him to stay, and that he hadn’t exactly done much better than me at working out what to do. It turned into a proper shouting match, with him accusing me of not caring enough about his family and me telling him he didn’t understand what it was like carrying this on my shoulders.

Hermione tried to stop us, took my side, and begged him to take the locket off and calm down. Instead, he said he was leaving. He actually packed his things. Hermione ran after him, sobbing, and asked him to stay, said she’d go with him if he stayed. He told her he thought she’d choose him, and when she didn’t, he Disapparated, and it was just Hermione and me left in the tent.

instances.Reference_Time: Book 5, Chapter 26, After dinner on Monday night
instances.Gold_Response:
I met Cho in the entrance hall and we walked down to Hogsmeade, and it was all right at first, a bit awkward but not terrible. She suggested we go into Madam Puddifoot’s, which turned out to be this horribly frilly, steamy little tea shop crammed with snogging couples and lurid pink stuff everywhere, and I could barely move my elbows without hitting someone.

We sat there with cherubs chucking confetti on our heads, and I couldn’t think of anything sensible to say. Cho started talking about Cedric and how everyone kept bringing him up, and then she started crying and saying people expected her to be over it and that I must want to talk about him too, and I just sat there like an idiot handing her napkins and not knowing what to say that wouldn’t make it worse.

Then I told her I had to meet Hermione later to talk about something important, and that was when it really went wrong. Cho got angry and jealous, asking why I was seeing Hermione, whether I fancied her, why Hermione had written to her before Christmas, all that. I tried to explain it was about the Defence group and even said she could come along if she liked, which only made her more upset, like I was trying to drag Hermione into our date.

In the end she was crying and furious and saying I should go off to meet Hermione, and she stormed out of the shop. I sat there for a bit feeling completely useless, then paid and left to go and find Hermione, knowing the whole thing had been a complete disaster.

She went spare about me going off alone and accused me of walking straight into a trap, said it could’ve been sent by a Death Eater. I argued that it was a Patronus, so it had to be protective magic, not Dark, and that whoever sent it must be on our side. We went back and forth about whether it could somehow be Dumbledore, or someone working for him, but we still had no idea whose Patronus it actually was.

I found out he wasn’t just the perfect hero I’d always imagined. From what Sirius and Lupin told me, when he was my age he could be a right arrogant git – showing off, hexing people like Snape just because he was bored, strutting around because he was good at Quidditch and popular. They admitted he and Sirius were pretty much bullies back then.

They also said he grew out of it – that by seventh year he’d stopped hexing people who couldn’t defend themselves, that he “deflated his head a bit,” became a better person, and that was when Mum finally agreed to go out with him. So I learnt he’d been stupid and nasty at fifteen, but that he changed later and wasn’t just that person forever.

instances.Gold_Response:
I was in the hospital wing because Ron, Hermione, and I went through the trapdoor to stop Snape—well, who we thought was Snape—getting the Stone.

We got past Fluffy with the flute, then I dropped through the trapdoor into the Devil’s Snare, flew after the right key in that room full of winged keys, and helped Ron with that gigantic chess set where he got knocked out. After that, I went on alone because Ron was unconscious and Hermione had to go back to get help.

I passed the troll that was already knocked out, then had that logic puzzle with the bottles so I could get through the black fire. In the last chamber I found Quirrell instead of Snape, and Voldemort was… there, with him, on the back of his head. Quirrell tried to use me to get the Stone from the Mirror of Erised, but somehow it ended up in my pocket. When he attacked me, my hands burned him whenever I touched him. Everything went mad—he was screaming, Voldemort rushed at me, there was terrible pain in my scar, and then I blacked out.

Next thing I remember properly, I woke up in the hospital wing.
